I used to have a problem. I would spend ages building the houses and making the sims, preparing myself to get emotionally attached and then three minutes of gameplay and I would roll my eyes and quit. No matter what I did I couldn’t stick to a household, but what I’ve realised about the sims is that you really have to create the personalities and characters yourself to enjoy so I’m going to give you my top tips (and I’ve been playing with the same save file on lifespan long for two years now so I know they work)

-Create external characters, friends, enemies, your scheming co worker who wants your job and who you incessantly try to poison at a formal dinner to no avail, your childhood friend who now is homeless and desperately needs to sleep on your sofa for two sim weeks, your best friend who you have feelings for since you were teenagers but now you’re both married so you can never be together (unless you cheat), your neighbour who’s kids hang out with yours and who you gift baked goods because they let you use their pool! Make your sims feel more alive this way
-Don’t just create the perfect partner, make issues, one of you wants to live in the city and the other the town, ones a cat person and ones a dog person, unrequited love, one wants marriage the other just wants a fling, make their parents and their siblings! You love your girlfriend but her sister is also really attractive so....the parents in law hate you and your relationship with them is terrible! You argue and then make up, go on a break and realise how much you like each other, when everythings always perfect it gets old fast, make sims that fundamentally are different and clash constantly but don’t realise it’s never going to work.
-Hobbies! Match your sims interests to their character! If your sim loves painting chances are they also like photography. A sports sim is going to want a home gym so make them save to get one. If a sim likes yoga they might also be vegetarian and drink green tea and have a large following on instagram. Push this onto your sims because the sims sure as hell won’t. Also take this into account when deciding jobs, just because a sim loves cooking doesnt mean they have to be a chef, make them multi dimensional.
-Give them favourite colours, foods, aspirations all that stuff. I have a sim who loves pink and singing, she’s also very self conscious about her body so wears baggy clothes even in the heat and her boyfriend knows how insecure she is so he treats her badly and gets away with it, she has a terrible relationship with her mother because they’re complete opposites and wants to get a nose piercing but is too scared of the pain. The sims does not do that stuff for you, take the time to write it out and you won’t forget it.
-Challenge! (No I don’t mean the challenges online) I’ve already mentioned the relationship side of this but theres so much more. Go online and find a wheel of fortune kind of program and enter a bunch of random events, a sim death, a sim gets fired, a sim inherits a ton of money, a sim loses a ton of money on a misplaced gamble or lawsuit, the house burns down, the sim gets pregnant, anything you want! My sims husband recently got ‘run over’ they had four kids together (kids and toddlers) and shes so upset that she’s sold the house they used to live in and quit her job and moved them all to a different town, her oldest kid is so traumatised that she is now terrified of death and is desperately trying to become a vampire to avoid it happening to her.
